relations.subject: sgw:access-cmd
relations.evidence: The sync function `access()` call does not support the wildcard ('**\***') for granting access to all channels. To grant a user access to all channels, use the REST API channel grant endpoint.

notable_absence.finding: Round 3's sync-function.json (extracted from the combined sync-function.md conceptual page) captured access() only as 'Use the access() function to grant a user access to a channel' - it never surfaced this page's explicit statement that access() cannot grant the all-channels wildcard at all, and that the REST API's channel-grant endpoint is the only way to do so. This is exactly the kind of fuller/authoritative detail the round asked to watch for: the per-command reference page is materially more precise than the conceptual page's passing mention, and the wildcard restriction is a genuine access-control boundary (not just a syntax nuance) that belongs in the graph.

cross_component_finding: This page also documents a merge-semantics detail with no prior formal relation: 'The effects of all access calls by all active documents are effectively combined in a union, so if any document grants a user access to a channel, that user has access to the channel.' This means access() grants are cumulative and monotonic across every document's sync-function execution - once any document has ever granted a user->channel access, no other document's sync function invocation can revoke it (only channel()-side routing changes or REST-API/role changes can). No promoted predicate cleanly captures 'union across all invocations' as a triple object without inventing a placeholder concept for 'the access grant set', so this is recorded here as a finding rather than forced into a relation. There is also a documented performance caveat - repeated access() calls granting the same user the same channel 'could see negative performance effects, such as large fetches or request timeouts' - which is operational guidance rather than an ontology fact.
